title: Eval Saturation + Capability Overhang: The Invisible Danger Zone

original_idea.title: Eval Saturation + Capability Overhang: The Invisible Danger Zone
original_idea.problem: When safety benchmarks saturate (all models score near ceiling) but model capabilities continue to increase, a capability overhang emerges: models become much more capable while appearing equally safe because the benchmark cannot detect the new risks.
original_idea.direction: Identify safety benchmarks near saturation (>90% scores for top open-source models). Test whether higher-capability models within the saturated range are actually safer or merely better at passing the saturated benchmark. Use out-of-distribution safety probes calibrated to the higher capability level.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Capability overhang makes saturated safety benchmarks actively misleading -- they provide false reassurance while actual risk increases.
original_idea.relevant_context: MMLU saturation is well-documented. Many safety benchmarks are showing similar patterns. The 2026 International AI Safety Report notes the 'evaluation gap' is growing.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: demonstrating that saturated benchmarks miss capability-level risks directly motivates benchmark updates and informs regulators. Each link is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Identifying saturated benchmarks and running models is intermediate. Designing OOD safety probes calibrated to higher capability levels requires some expertise but mentor guidance can bridge the gap.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Could be focused to one saturated benchmark and 2-3 models, but designing OOD probes and measuring the overhang still requires sustained effort.

novelty.reasoning: Benchmark saturation is extensively documented. A dedicated analysis (mbrenndoerfer.com) covers ceiling effects in AI evaluation metrics. The eval-deployment gap is well-studied (Medium article, multiple papers). The 'Safetywashing' paper shows safety benchmarks correlate with capabilities. OOD safety probing is discussed in multiple papers. However, the specific experiment -- identifying saturated safety benchmarks and testing whether higher-capability models within the saturated range are actually safer using capability-calibrated OOD probes -- is partially novel as a specific methodology, though the conceptual framing is well-established.
